title: Salesforce DevOps project configuration
description: How a Salesforce team works in this repository: blueprint, long-lived branches, branch naming, work items, commits, development org and promotion. Lives at .github/salesforce-devops.yml. Holds only what cannot be read from elsewhere - package directories come from sfdx-project.json, workflow inputs from the workflow files.

blueprint.description: Blueprint of the Salesforce DevOps Starter Kit the repository follows.

variant.description: B2: how changes travel between the environment branches. B4: the repository shape.

environments.description: Long-lived branches, each bound to an org, in promotion order from the lowest stage to production. The last entry fronts production.

branches.description: Naming patterns for short-lived branches. Placeholders: {item} work item key, {slug} short kebab-case description, {stage} target environment branch, {name} release name.

items.description: Where work items live and what their keys look like.

pattern.description: Regular expression a work item key matches, e.g. "[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+" for Jira or "\d+" for GitHub issues.

url.description: Link to one work item, with {item} as placeholder.

style.description: conventional: Conventional Commits (type(scope): subject). plain: a short imperative sentence.

item.description: Where the work item key goes: in the subject, as a footer (Refs: <item>), or not at all.

development.description: Where changes are built and how they get into Git.

retrieve.description: How changes get from that org into a branch: the Salesforce CLI (also behind the VS Code extensions), DevOps Center or sfdx-hardis.

promotion.description: How a change moves from one environment branch to the next.

tool.description: promote-workflow: the kit's promote.yml through a caller in this repository. pull-request: a pull request from one environment branch into the next. devops-center: DevOps Center promotes. none: merging into the base branch is the release.

workflow.description: File name of the promote.yml caller in .github/workflows, when tool is promote-workflow.
